messages:
Alex N.: Heads up — observed a kv-cache + tokenizer mismatch when the router falls back from dedicated-prod -> hosted-quantized in eu-west for customer tier `standard`. Outputs differ and tool-calling sometimes drops. Can we treat this as a compatibility gap in the fallback matrix?
Priya S.: @Alex N. can you paste the smallest repro? which model variants exactly?
Alex N.: repro attached in prod logs (short): `req: model=redwood-13b-ded, fallback=redwood-13b-q4`, prefix tokens get truncated, tool_call fields missing. Happens under quota throttle spike.
Liam: this smells like two separate issues: tokenizer vocabulary/ids mismatch OR KV cache offset bug when sequence_len != cached_len. Also fallback path strips out `tool_call` in our internal response marshalling.
Marta: from a quota/console POV, when we route to hosted fallback we should surface that the customer is on degraded model and whether tool-calls are preserved. UX currently just says "degraded" which is vague.
Jamie: agreed — rollout UX needs a per-request telemetry flag: `fallback_reason` + `parity_flags` so SRE and customers can filter traces. Also dashboard needs column for `tool_call_parity` and `tokenizer_parity`.
Tobias: operational policy question: should fallback be allowed for `standard` tier by default, or only for `burst`? If we block fallback for some tiers we'll need a quota override flow.
Priya S.: quick check: tokenizer mismatch only if the hosted variant uses an updated tokenizer (we shipped tokenpatch v2 to hosted only). If true, fallback should be blocked or transcoded.
Alex N.: confirmed hosted uses tokenpatch v2 in eu-west. That explains the ID drift. But why does tool_call drop? logs show marshaller received `tools:[]` from runtime for fallback variant.
Liam: runtime-team note: when we switch kernels for q4 quantized variants we run a different postproc path that currently bypasses function schemas. I'll open an issue.
eng-alert-bot: [alert] 1969993001 - fallback-rate spike observed for eu-west standard during quota-rebalance. 1500 fallbacks in 10m.
Marta: that spike is the root cause — quota rebalance triggered fallback en masse. Need a console banner and per-customer breadcrumb in usage view. Also need to update billing docs if fallbacks change inference token counts.
Jamie: action items: 1) Priya/Runtime: verify tokenizer mapping or add on-the-fly transcoder; 2) Runtime: preserve `tool_call` schema in fallback marshaller; 3) Platform: add `fallback_reason` telemetry tag + dashboard columns; 4) Product: decision on tier-level fallback policy (Tobias).
Tobias: I'll schedule a quick sync with product legal & sales — big accounts will expect deterministic tool-calling. Propose default: allow fallback for premium/prod-safety tiers only with explicit opt-in for standard.
Priya S.: I'll prototype a token-transcoder shim that maps v1->v2 ids at the router. Low risk but will add ~0.8ms per request. Will surface perf tradeoff in console.
Liam: created issue RUN-4927 for marshaller parity, tagging @runtime.
Alex N.: thanks. please tag the compatibility matrix doc when you update it. Current matrix doesn't list tokenpatch v2 divergence.
Jamie: I'll add `tokenizer_version` and `tool_call_supported` columns to the matrix table in the console docs and wire telemetry filters.
eng-alert-bot: [note] 1969994000 - ticket RUN-4927 created by Liam; linked to this thread.
Marta: filing a small UX ticket to show fallback details on the customer's model page. We should also add a tooltip that explains the perf & parity tradeoffs.
Tobias: fine-grain rollout strategy: canary fallback in ap-south (low risk) then EU, US; block for top-10 customers until we validate tool parity.
Alex N.: quick question: do we want automated rollback when tool_call parity regression > 1% on eval set? sounds reasonable.
Jamie: yes — add a rollout policy rule: auto-unroute if parity_degradation_rate > 1% over 30m.
Priya S.: I'll run a small eval set across variants and post numbers later today.
Alex N.: great. I'll update the compatibility matrix doc and ping the runtime team. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
